{{technical|date=September 2010}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''quantaloid''' is a [[category (mathematics)|category]] [[enriched category|enriched]] over the category '''Sup''' of [[Complete lattice#Morphisms of complete lattices|complete lattices with supremum-preserving maps]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Rosenthal | first = Kimmo I.
 | isbn = 0-582-29440-1
 | mr = 1427263
 | publisher = Longman, Harlow
 | series = Pitman Research Notes in Mathematics Series
 | title = The theory of quantaloids
 | volume = 348
 | year = 1996}}. See in particular [https://books.google.com/books?id=O3bno8HpcFAC&pg=PA15 p.&nbsp;15].</ref> In other words, for any [[object (category theory)|objects]] ''a'' and ''b'' the [[Morphism#Hom-set|Hom]] object between them is not just a [[set (mathematics)|set]] but a complete [[Lattice (order)|lattice]], in such a way that composition of morphisms preserves all joins:
:<math>(\bigvee_i f_i) \circ (\bigvee_j g_j) = \bigvee_{i,j} (f_i \circ g_j) </math>

The [[endomorphism]] lattice <math>\mathrm{Hom}(X,X)</math> of any object <math>X</math> in a quantaloid is a [[quantale]], whence the name.
